official_skills.notes: NOT a skill - it is an MCP server that serves Astro documentation on demand. Recorded here because it is the Astro team's only agent-facing artifact for people building with Astro, and the mentor should say it exists. The install route was not confirmed on 2026-09-11.
Community, not the Astro team. 44 stars on 2026-09-11. Install route unconfirmed. Present it as an option with that caveat, never as doctrine.

gap_map.gap: skills for people building WITH Astro
gap_map.why_it_matters: The withastro org publishes 22 SKILL.md files and every one of them is maintainer tooling - triage, releases, changesets, PR review, and an astro-developer skill whose own description says 'developing in the Astro monorepo'. None teaches you to build a site. Aggregator sites list these as 'Astro skills', which is how a search leads you to install contributor tooling.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor applies the architecture block below, which is verified against the Astro team's own documentation, and says plainly that no builder-facing skill exists.

gap_map.why_it_matters: Astro documents four runners and the Container API but takes no position on what deserves a test. The stack's own failure mode makes this worse: a component can render perfectly server-side and never hydrate, so the markup assertion passes while the button does nothing.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor applies the testing rules below.

layers.name: unit (Container API)
layers.belongs_here: an .astro component rendered to a string and asserted on - added in Astro 4.9.0 and the team's own answer for testing Astro components natively
layers.does_not_belong_here: anything that needs a browser or hydration
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the assertion is about behaviour after a click

layers.name: island unit
layers.belongs_here: the React/Vue/Svelte component inside an island, tested with that framework's own tooling
layers.does_not_belong_here: whether the island actually hydrates on the page

layers.name: e2e
layers.belongs_here: that an island hydrates and responds to a real click, and the flows whose breakage is an incident. Playwright, Cypress and Nightwatch are all documented.
layers.cost: slowest; but it is the only layer that proves hydration happened

testing.proportions: No proportions stated by the Astro team. They do state one rule that changes where tests run: 'Run your tests against your production code to more closely resemble your live, deployed site.'
rules: Run tests against the production build, not the dev server. The Astro team says so explicitly, and dev and production differ in how islands are served.
Use the Container API to unit-test .astro components: render to a string and assert on the output. It is the team's own mechanism, available since 4.9.0.
At least one end-to-end test per interactive island proves it HYDRATES. Nothing below that layer can prove it - the markup is identical whether the directive is there or not.
astro check is the typecheck for .astro files. A green unit suite with a failing astro check is not a green project.
Read package.json before assuming a runner: Vitest, Playwright, Cypress and Nightwatch are all documented options.
traps: THE Astro trap: a component that renders correctly server-side but has no client:* directive produces identical HTML to one that does. Every markup assertion passes and the button does nothing. Only a real browser catches it.
Testing against the dev server instead of the build - the team warns about this directly.
An island that works alone and breaks on the page because two islands ship two different framework runtimes.
client:visible islands never hydrate in a test viewport that never scrolls them into view, so the test reports a dead component as working-as-designed.
Content and assets in public/ are copied untouched, so a broken path there fails silently in production while every test passes.
what_not_to_test: That Astro stripped the client JavaScript - that is the framework's contract.
That a file in src/pages became a route.
The exact HTML string of a layout; it changes on every markup edit.
Generated types in .astro/ and build output in dist/.
testing.notes: The Container API covers .astro components; islands are tested with their own framework's tooling. Neither proves hydration - only a browser does.

growth_thresholds.extract_shared_component: >=3 occurrences of the same markup across >=2 pages
growth_thresholds.review_island_budget: >3 client:load islands on one page - client:load blocks, and shipping several defeats the reason to be on Astro at all (mentor threshold, not the Astro team's)
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 sites or apps import the same internal module

architecture.pattern: islands architecture - static HTML by default, JavaScript opted into one component at a time

layers.name: src/pages
layers.holds: the routes. Required, and the ONLY directory Astro reserves - the docs say so verbatim: 'the only directory reserved by Astro is src/pages/'
layers.must_not: hold anything non-routable; a file dropped here becomes a page

layers.name: src/components
layers.holds: reusable units, .astro or a UI framework component
layers.must_not: be treated as mandatory - the docs call it 'a common convention in Astro projects, but it is not required'

layers.name: src/layouts
layers.must_not: hold page-specific logic; also a convention, not required

layers.name: client island
layers.holds: the interactive component, opted in with a client:* directive
layers.must_not: become the default - Astro strips all client JavaScript unless you explicitly ask for it, and that is the whole performance story

layers.name: server island
layers.holds: expensive or slow server-side work deferred with server:defer so the page renders immediately around it
layers.must_not: exist before something is actually slow

layers.name: public/
layers.holds: assets copied untouched at build time
layers.must_not: hold anything that needs optimisation or processing - that goes in src/

variants.name: The documented convention: components/, layouts/, styles/, images/
variants.use_when: the default, and what every Astro tutorial looks like
variants.cost: these are type-based folders, so one feature's page, component and style end up in three places

variants.name: Feature folders beside src/pages
variants.use_when: features are independent and each owns its components and styles
variants.cost: you leave the layout newcomers recognise from the docs

variants.name: Reserved-only: just src/pages, everything else however you like
variants.cost: nothing stops it drifting; the discipline is entirely social

rules: src/pages is the only directory Astro reserves. A file placed there becomes a route - never put non-routable code in it.

Everything renders to HTML with client-side JavaScript stripped automatically. A component runs in the browser ONLY if you write a client:* directive on it. The docs put the burden on you explicitly: 'it is up to you as the developer to explicitly tell Astro which components on the page need to also run in the browser'.

Every client:* directive is a decision, not a formality: client:load runs immediately, client:idle waits for the browser, client:visible waits for the viewport. Pick by when the user actually needs it.

Start with the default static output. The Astro team's own words: 'Start with the default static mode until you are sure that most or all of your pages will be rendered on demand.' Add an adapter only when a route genuinely needs it.
public/ is copied untouched. Anything that should be optimised goes in src/.
Do not add a server island until something is measurably slow. server:defer exists for expensive work, and adding it early is the over-abstraction signal.
architecture.component_library: Promote to a shared component at >=3 occurrences across >=2 pages. On Astro the bar is lower than elsewhere for a different reason: a shared .astro component costs zero client JavaScript, so the usual 'is the abstraction worth it' tradeoff loses its performance half.
architecture.notes: Astro prescribes routing and hydration and leaves organisation open - the same shape as Next.js. src/pages is reserved; components/, layouts/, styles/ and images/ are explicitly described as conventions that are not required. So the mentor's job is not to impose a layout, it is to make sure one is chosen, written down and followed.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Astro prerenders everything by default. Switching to output: 'server' requires an adapter and changes where the site can be deployed.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Static. The Astro team says to start there until you are sure most pages need on-demand rendering.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Going server-first without needing it gives up the reason to be on Astro; discovering you need on-demand late means picking a host and adapter under deadline.

key_decisions.decision: Which UI framework runs inside the islands
key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Astro is framework-agnostic and ships none by default. React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Preact are all first-class.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: None, until something is genuinely interactive. Then one - the one the team already knows.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Two frameworks on one page ship two runtimes to the browser, which is exactly the cost Astro exists to avoid.

key_decisions.decision: Which client:* directive each island gets
key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: There is no default. An island with no directive never hydrates and looks identical in the HTML.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: client:visible for anything below the fold, client:idle for the rest, client:load only for something the user touches immediately.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: client:load on everything turns an Astro site into a slow SPA. Forgetting the directive ships a dead component that every test passes.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Which on-demand features work depends on the adapter, and the adapter depends on where it runs.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: A static host until on-demand rendering is genuinely needed.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Building on a runtime feature the chosen adapter does not support is discovered at deploy time.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Only src/pages is reserved. Everything else is a convention the docs describe and explicitly do not require.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: The documented convention, so newcomers recognise it.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: The failure is not the wrong layout, it is an inconsistent one - half by feature and half by type, so nobody can predict where a file lives.

dead_code_risks: Files in src/pages are routes, reachable by filesystem convention and never imported
Components referenced only from .astro templates, which import-graph tools do not follow
Assets in public/ referenced by a string path
Content collection entries discovered by directory scan
Framework islands referenced only through a client:* directive in a template
Adapter and integration code activated only by astro.config
